name: Partial reprogramming skin patch
subtitle: a patch that winds old skin partly back

effects.effect: four genes turn an adult cell back into a stem cell that can become any tissue
a cell follows genes put into it

effect: four genes turn an adult cell back into a stem cell that can become any tissue
how: Old skin heals so slowly that a bedsore or a diabetic ulcer can cost an elderly person a leg, and nothing on the shelf makes skin young again. The patch's hair-fine needles deliver a brief pulse of the four genes that turn adult cells back toward stem cells, on for three days and off for three weeks, so cells recover a young cell's chemistry without forgetting what kind of cell they are. A timer chip enforces the off period, because duration is the whole safety margin.
obstacle: Leave those genes on too long and cells forget themselves and grow tumours; the safe window has to hold for years, not weeks.
why: Puts mouse rejuvenation in a dosable device where the off-switch is mechanical.
real: Pulsed OSKM reprogramming in skin is established in mice — mosaic partial epidermal reprogramming healed wounds faster with less scarring including in diabetic conditions (Nature Communications, 2026), and intradermal AAV-OSK improved healing in aged mice — but delivery is genetic or viral and no microneedle patch with an on/off timer has been demonstrated.
